pairs.why: Both tables could stand, but A's broad pedestal and stepped base hold its top more solidly than B's thin column under a small slab, so A only slightly.
A's yoke hangs from the truss clamp and pivots on both sides of the lamp body, while B's U-yoke attaches only on one side and its left arm ends in the air.
A's keys are blank, so the calculator can't be used, while B has labelled digit and operator keys like the real card.
A's rock is a soft blob with holes that look like they go all the way through, while B reads as a solid cratered rock with a flame trail streaming behind it.
B has four wheels on axles, a front tongue and a canvas cover with a proper opening, while A's oversized two wheels and dark hole of a cover opening make an unclear, cart-like build.
B's loop is knotted to the tied coil in a way that could hold, while in A the loop ends at a loose ferrule and tangles into the coil, though neither shows a proper honda.
Both cats sit on the floor with attached legs, tail and collar, and neither has a build fault; they differ only in surface finish.
A's hands all share one centre hub and the clock sits flat against the wall, while B's red second hand pivots off-centre and the clock casts a floor shadow as if it were standing on the ground.
